problem.heading: Token limits should not stop your flow.
problem.body: Cloud agents bill you for thinking. Freevobe runs the model you already have, so the meter never starts.

items.detail: Your GPU does the work. No rate limits, no weekly caps and no waiting for a reset at midnight.
One local model, unlimited prompts. The only cost is the electricity you already pay for.

givesBack.heading: No ads. A choice to give back.
givesBack.body: Freevobe does not sell your attention. Instead of an advertising slot, the app can offer a voluntary reminder about a cause you picked. You give directly to the organisation — Freevobe never handles the money.
givesBack.badge: No ad network, no tracking, no checkout in the app.

principles.title: No advertising
principles.body: Freevobe ships without ad slots, ad scripts and ad networks. Nothing in the app is for sale.

principles.title: No money through Freevobe
principles.body: The app has no checkout, no account and no payment provider. Every link opens the organisation’s own page.

principles.title: Off by default
principles.body: The reminder in the chat is opt-in, appears in its own block and never touches the agent’s context.

principles.title: Your log stays local

faq.heading: Questions, answered.
faq.body: Still curious? The docs cover the agent loop, skills and MCP in detail.

items.question: What does “vobe” mean?
items.answer: To vobe is to build with Ollama through natural language — locally and without token limits. It is vibe coding, minus the meter running.

items.question: Do I need an API key?
items.answer: No. Freevobe connects directly to your local Ollama installation.

items.question: Which models can I use?
items.answer: Any model available in your local Ollama installation — Qwen, Llama, DeepSeek, Mistral, Gemma and whatever you pull next.

items.question: Does my code leave my computer?
items.answer: Not by default. Freevobe is local-first: the agent, the model and your files run on your machine. A cloud model is only used if you connect one yourself.

items.question: Is Freevobe free?
items.answer: The core app is free to use with your own local Ollama models.

phone.title: The phone app
phone.body: Freevobe Mobile mirrors the desktop app: QR-pair once over your local network and then follow runs, diffs and approvals from the couch. Nothing leaves your Wi-Fi — the phone talks to the Freevobe agent running on your own machine.
phone.step1: Download the APK and open it. Android asks you to allow installs from this source — the file is not from Google Play.
phone.step2: Open the desktop app and show the pairing QR code. Point the phone at it.
phone.step3: Both devices need to be on the same network. Pairing works offline.
phone.ios: iOS builds are not published yet — they need a Mac and an Apple Developer account.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Freevobe is local-first. This page describes what this website and the Freevobe desktop app do with your data.

sections.title: This website
paragraphs: This site is a static page. It sets no analytics, no tracking pixels and no cookies of its own, and it makes no requests to third-party hosts — fonts and images are served from the same domain.
Your theme choice (dark or light) is stored in your browser's local storage so the page opens the way you left it. It never leaves your machine.

sections.title: Advertising and Gives Back
paragraphs: Freevobe has no advertising: no ad slots, no ad scripts and no ad network. The website and the desktop app therefore set no advertising cookies or device identifiers, and no data is shared with a third party for marketing.

In place of an ad slot, the desktop app can show a voluntary reminder about a charity — Freevobe Gives Back. It is off until you turn it on. The reminder contains a link to the organisation's own website; Freevobe has no checkout, no account and no payment provider, and never receives or forwards a donation.
If you record a contribution in the app, the note stays in your local database and is labelled as self-reported. It is never sent to the organisation or to us, and you can delete it at any time.

sections.title: The desktop app
bullets: Your code, prompts and files are processed on your own machine by a model you run yourself through Ollama. Nothing is uploaded by default.
Sessions, project indexes and memory are stored in a local SQLite database on your computer.
The app sends no telemetry. There is no account and no sign-in.
A cloud model is only contacted if you configure one yourself, and that connection is then governed by the provider you chose.

sections.title: Downloads
paragraphs: Download links point to the project's release page. Your browser and the hosting provider of that page apply their own normal request logging.

sections.title: Changes
paragraphs: If this policy changes, the date at the top of this page changes with it. Freevobe is open source, so this page and its history are reviewable in the public repository.

terms.metaDescription: Plain terms for using Freevobe and this website.
terms.title: Terms
terms.intro: Short and plain: Freevobe is free software that runs on your hardware, and you are responsible for what you build with it.

sections.title: The app
bullets: The core application is free to use with your own local Ollama models. There is no subscription, no token metering and no usage limit imposed by us.
The source code is released under the MIT licence. You may use, modify and redistribute it under that licence.
The app runs on your machine with your credentials and your files. You are responsible for the projects you point it at, the commands you approve and the changes you commit.

sections.title: No warranty
paragraphs: Freevobe is provided “as is”, without warranty of any kind. Model output can be wrong, and generated code should be reviewed like any other contribution. Keep your work under version control and review diffs before approving them.

sections.title: Models and third-party services
paragraphs: Models you run through Ollama, and any service you choose to connect, are governed by their own terms and licences. We do not control and are not responsible for them.

sections.title: This website
paragraphs: Product information here is provided for orientation and may change as the app evolves. Material may be served by advertising partners in the future; see the privacy page for what that means for your data.
